'''Ishikiri Tsurugiya Shrine''' (石切劔箭神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|en|Shinto|qid=Q812767|lt=Shinto}} shrine located in {{ill|Higashiōsaka|ar|هيغاشي-أوساكا (أوساكا)|az|Hiqaşiosaka|ban|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|bg|Хигашиосака|ca|Higashi-Ōsaka|ce|Хигасиосака|ceb|Higashiōsaka Shi|cs|Higašiósaka|cy|Higashiōsaka|de|Higashiōsaka|eo|Higaŝiosaka|es|Higashiōsaka (Osaka)|et|Higashiōsaka|eu|Higashiōsaka|fa|هیگاشی‌اوساکا، اوساکا|fi|Higashi-Ōsaka|fr|Higashiōsaka|ga|Higashiōsaka|gl|Higashiōsaka|he|היגשיאוסקה|hy|Հիգասիոսակա|id|Higashiōsaka|it|Higashiōsaka|ja|東大阪市|ko|히가시오사카시|ms|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|mzn|هیگاشی‌اوساکا، اوساکا|nl|Higashiosaka|no|Higashiōsaka|pl|Higashiōsaka|pt|Higashiosaka|ro|Higashiōsaka|ru|Хигасиосака|sh|Higasiosaka|simple|Higashiōsaka|sr|Хигашиосака|sv|Higashiōsaka|tg|Ҳигашиосака|th|ฮิงาชิโอซากะ|tl|Higashiōsaka|tr|Higashiōsaka|tt|Хигасиосака|tum|Higashiōsaka|uk|Хіґасіосака|ur|ہیگاشیوساکا، اوساکا|vi|Higashiōsaka|war|Higashiōsaka, Osaka|zh|東大阪市|zh_classical|東大阪市|zh_min_nan|Higasiôsaka-chhī|zh_yue|東大阪|qid=Q243863|lt=Higashiōsaka}}, Osaka Prefecture. It is affiliated with {{ill|Shintō Ishikiri Sect|ja|神道石切教}} and is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} of Kawachi District. The shrine is locally known as "Ishikiri-san" or "The God of Tumors."

== History ==
The shrine is famous for its {{ill|Ohyakudo-mairi|ja|お百度参り}}, a ritual involving repetitive prayer walks between two sacred stones. Its precise founding date is unclear due to a fire that destroyed most records and the treasure repository. However, the Kizumi family, hereditary shrine caretakers, attribute the origin to the 2nd year of Emperor Jimmu's reign (659 BCE) when Kami-musubi-no-mikoto enshrined Nigi-hayahi at Mount Miyama. During Emperor Sujin's reign, the shrine was relocated to its current site.

The shrine appears in historical records such as the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}, which notes that in 865 (Jōgan 7), it was conferred the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. It is also listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}.

The shrine faced significant destruction during the late {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}} due to conflict, including the burning of its Buddhist temple, {{ill|Hōtsū-ji|ja|法通寺}}. It was later rebuilt, and its rituals were restored, but many original features were moved to the current Kamino-sha.

In the modern period, it was classified as a village shrine. In 1905 (Meiji 38), Nigi-hayahi was officially enshrined in the main sanctuary. Post-war, the shrine established the Shintō Ishikiri Sect as its religious headquarters. A branch shrine, "Ishikiri Tokyo Bunshi," was founded in 1975 in Tokyo.

== Deities ==
* {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日尊|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}} (Nigi-hayahi-no-mikoto)
* {{ill|Umashimaji|ja|可美真手命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qid=Q10946169}} (Kami-musubi-no-mikoto), the son of Nigi-hayahi.
These are collectively referred to as "Ishikiri Daimyōjin."

== festivals ==
* '''October 22 – Autumn Grand Festival''': A ceremony of gratitude for the year's harvest, featuring the purification ritual "Miyu Kagura." During the festival, the shrine treasures are displayed to the public.
* '''December 31 – Year-End Purification Ceremony''': Participants cleanse sins and impurities through rituals like {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|fa|اوهارائه‌شیکی|fr|Ōharae-shiki|ja|大祓|ko|오하라에|simple|Ōharae-shiki|qid=Q11261910}}.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* '''Tachi Sword ("Ishikiri-maru")''' – Forged by {{ill|Sanjō Yukiie|ja|三条有成}}.

=== Osaka City Natural Monuments ===
* '''Camphor Tree''' at Ishikiri Tsurugiya Shrine.

== Access ==
* '''Main Shrine''': 7 minutes' walk from {{ill|Shin-Ishikiri Station|en|Shin-Ishikiri Station|qid=Q7497096|lt=Shin-Ishikiri Station}} (Kintetsu Keihanna Line) or 15 minutes from {{ill|Ishikiri Station|en|Ishikiri Station|qid=Q6080325|lt=Ishikiri Station}} (Kintetsu Nara Line).
* '''Kamino-sha''': 7 minutes' walk from Ishikiri Station, about 1 km east of the Main Shrine.
